problem: The game was not succeeding as a business.
title: Tiny Speck shuts down its game Glitch and ships its internal chat tool as Slack
context: Tiny Speck built an online game called Glitch and developed an internal chat tool along the way.
decision_made: Shut down Glitch and turn the internal communication tool into a product called Slack.
action_taken: Glitch closed in December 2012; a July 2013 memo to the team, "We Don't Sell Saddles Here", set out how to position Slack.
observed_outcome: Not documented in the sources used.
lessons: A tool built for internal use can become the real product when the original idea does not work.
limitations: Only the pivot and the positioning memo were checked here, not results. The memo is not the pivot announcement.

claims.claim_text: Tiny Speck shut down Glitch in December 2012 and shipped its internal chat tool as Slack.
A July 2013 memo to the team argued Slack was selling a reduction in information overload rather than chat software.
